headline: Leafs’ John Tavares week-to-week with lower-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Toronto's John Tavares is week-to-week with a lower-body injury, after he left Thursday's 5-4 overtime loss to the Sabres following a collision with Norris that sent him to the ice.

The loss matters less for Tavares's production than for how the Leafs have been playing. TOR has been outplayed so far this season, with a 44.6% share of expected goals (44% at five-on-five), and has been rescued by results: +3.4 goals above expected and +3.6 goals saved above expected. Tavares's own numbers are shaky. He has just a 29.91% five-on-five expected goals share over 7 games, and TOR's share is 18.52 points worse with him on the ice. His 7 points (2 goals, 5 assists) are in line with his 2.5 expected goals, and he is only 0.5 goals under that mark. At 16.52 minutes a game, his absence is not a clear hit to the Leafs' chance creation, but a team already living on goaltending and finishing luck has little margin if his minutes go to someone worse. Fantasy owners should treat this as a short-term stash decision, since last season's 31 goals and 71 points look like a long way off for now.
